subject: Re: Expansion pricing for Atlas Health - Clinical Insights workload
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Expansion: Clinical Insights — preliminary pricing options

Hi Maria,

Thanks again for the demo last week — super excited about Atlas's Clinical Insights roadmap. As we discussed, the new product will drive a different cost profile (longer generations for narrative summaries + heavy embedding traffic for search/recall). I sketched two pragmatic options so procurement has something concrete to evaluate.

Quick context: current hosted API commit is $30k/mo (baseline product workloads). The Clinical Insights pilot is expected to add ~1.6B tokens/mo and ~12M embedding calls at launch.

Option A — Incremental commit (clean, predictable)
- Add a dedicated incremental commit of $20k/mo for Clinical Insights (12‑month term)
- New workload receives a 15% per‑token discount above baseline rates; embeddings billed at 12% off list (separate bucket)
- 2 months of trial credits ($10k) to smooth onboarding

Option B — Hybrid ramp + burst credits (flexible initial ramp)
- 6‑month ramped commit: $10k/mo for months 1–3, $20k/mo months 4–6, then evaluate
- Burst bucket: $40k one‑time burst credits usable for spikes (expires 12 months)
- Blended discount: 10% on generative tokens, 8% on embeddings; larger discounts trigger once monthly usage exceeds 2M embeddings or 600M tokens

Governance & SLA notes: we can keep the workload on hosted API (no Dedicated capacity needed at pilot scale). SLA uplift (99.9% availability + 2x support response) can be added for an additional monthly platform fee — we can iterate on exact language.

I've attached a short commit matrix and a draft SOW so legal/procurement have line items to review. If you want, we can convert Option A into a 12‑month DocuSignable SOW next week.

Would love to hear procurement's pricing floor and preferred term length so we can land on something fast.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_commit_matrix.xlsx (xls, 48KB)]
[Attachment: Atlas_SOW_draft_v3.pdf (pdf, 240KB)]

From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@atlashealth.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@atlashealth.com
Date: 2027-09-15T11:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Expansion: Clinical Insights — preliminary pricing options

Hi Aisha,

Appreciate the clarity — this is a helpful starting point. A few questions from procurement and engineering:

1) Can you provide an expected blended unit price (USD per 1k tokens and per embedding) under Option A vs Option B? Procurement needs that for our cost model.
2) We prefer 12‑month minimums for commit lines. Would Atlas be able to convert Option B's ramp into a 12‑month guaranteed minimum (with the same front‑loaded payments)?
3) Embedding volume is a blocker — legal will want a clearer price trigger for the higher discounts (what exactly counts as "monthly usage exceeds 2M embeddings") and whether embeddings are metered per request or per vector.
4) PO and standard Net‑45 terms from our finance team — do you accept Net‑45? Any early‑payment discounts?

Procurement is open to a short pilot credit but needs to see the long‑term blended economics. If you can send a one‑page blended pricing table (tokens / embeddings / expected monthly spend) we can pass to finance/legal.

Thanks,
Maria
Director, Product Ops — Clinical Insights
Atlas Health

On Sep 14, 2027, at 9:12 AM, Aisha Rahman wrote:
> [Original message attached]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-16T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Pricing proposal for Atlas — internal pricing options

Aisha / Markus,

Notes from procurement reply — they want blended unit prices and Net‑45. Procurement prefers 12 months. Quick internal take:

- Margin guardrails: keep effective blended token revenue >= $0.012 per 1k tokens after discounts (we can flex if dataset skew reduces cost).
- Recommended public proposal: Offer Option A as the primary path but include a 12‑month convertible ramp clause for Option B (i.e., ramp becomes a 12‑month committed schedule if Atlas signs within 30 days).
- Embedding pricing: meter per embedding call (per vector returned). For the discounts, define triggers as calendar‑month totals; we should include a 10% buffer to avoid accidental slip.

Suggested draft language for external:
- Incremental commit: $20k/mo for 12 months; effective discounts: 15% tokens, 12% embeddings; 60‑day $10k pilot credit.
- Ramp convertible: 6‑month ramp becomes 12‑month at Atlas's option or automatically converts if average monthly usage in months 4–6 exceeds 80% of the committed ramp.

I'll attach a quick margin calc and recommended redlines. Markus: can you confirm we can accept Net‑45 for Atlas (they're a mid‑market healthcare customer)?

Laura
VP, Sales Operations

[Attachment: margin_note_atlas.xlsx (xls, 38KB)]

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-17T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Expansion: Clinical Insights — updated proposal and next steps

Hi Maria,

Thanks — sharing a concise blended table below and confirming a few governance items. If this looks good, I'll circulate a one‑page SOW and a DocuSign link for the 12‑month incremental commit path.

Blended pricing (illustrative) — Option A (12m incremental commit)
- Generative tokens: list $0.020 / 1k tokens -> 15% discount -> $0.017 / 1k (effective)
- Embeddings: list $0.030 / call -> 12% discount -> $0.0264 / call
- Expected monthly run‑rate at launch (Atlas estimate): 1.6B tokens (=> ~$27,200), 12M embeddings (=> ~$316,800 at list; discounted => ~$278k) — note: embeddings dominate cost; confirm whether you plan to vector compress/quantize.

Option B (convertible ramp)
- Month 1–3: $10k/mo (10% token / 8% embed discount)
- Month 4–6: $20k/mo (12% token / 10% embed discount)
- Conversion: ramp converts to a 12‑month committed schedule if months 4–6 average >= 80% of committed monthly spend.

Other answers:
- Embeddings are metered per API call that returns a vector; we'll add a glossary line in the SOW to reduce ambiguity.
- Net‑45 accepted; no standard early‑payment discount in the offer but we can discuss a 1% for Net‑15 on annual invoices if finance requests.
- SLA uplift and named support can be added as a line item in the SOW.

Next steps I propose:
1) I circulate a one‑page SOW for Option A (12m incremental commit) with the tables above.
2) You share procurement's preferred PO language and the contact for legal; we'll prep DocuSign.
3) Schedule a 30‑minute call early next week to run through the SOW and conversion clause.

If that works, I have the SOW ready to push live; attaching the SOW and the commit matrix again.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
